type III HLP is a rare but potentially serious cause of premature ASCVD in patients who also have a coexisting cause for hyperlipidemia.

type III hyperlipidemia is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder of lipoprotein and lipid metabolism, most frequently caused by homozygosity of the E2 allele of apolipoproteins E, and characterized by elevated plasma levels of triglyceride rich remnant lipoproteins, with associated increased risk of ASCVD and distinctive cutaneous xanthonomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the E2 isoforms are associated with a reduced risk of ASCVD when the apo E2 is present on normal apo B-containing lipoproteins, but that the presence of apo E2 on lipoproteins with atherogenic apo B is associated with an increased risk of ASCVD.
the dysbetalipoproteinaemia is an uncommon but distinctive and potentially important cause of premature ASCVD.

dysbetalipoproteinaemia is a genetic disorder of lipoprotein lipase (LPL)-mediated lipolysis of chylomicron remnants and very low-density lipoproteins (VLDL), which results in a failure to remove these remnants efficiently, and a consequent accumulation of cholesterol-rich lipoproteins in the circulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

type III HLP is an acquired disorder, which is most commonly associated with the presence of atherogenic lipoprotein remnants, which are generated by the lipolytic processing of chylomicrons and VLDL by lipoprotein lipase.
